Removing strict and extended dominance

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7000030
Type test case
has calculator text C_A = 10000; E_A = 4.0; C_B = 13000; E_B = 4.3; C_X = 20000; E_X = 4.4; C_C = 18000; E_C = 4.5; C_D = 22000; E_D = 4.8; ICER_B = 10000; ICER_D = 18000; frontier = A, B, D
has description in the module Five illustrative alternatives are measured in life-years. A costs £10,000 for 4.0, B costs £13,000 for 4.3, X costs £20,000 for 4.4, C costs £18,000 for 4.5 and D costs £22,000 for 4.8. Ordered by effect, X is strictly dominated by C, which costs less and produces more, so X is removed. The sequential ICERs are then £10,000 for B, £25,000 for C and approximately £13,333 for D per life-year gained. Because the ICER for C exceeds the ICER for D, C is extendedly dominated and removed. Recalculation gives £10,000 for B and £18,000 for D, which increase with effectiveness, so A, B and D form the frontier.
has module record identifier HE-EX-CEA-002
has test kind worked example
has title in the module Removing strict and extended dominance
has title key removing-strict-and-extended-dominance
isDefinedBy hemo-formulae.owlexternal

has description in the module Illustrative figures. The first procedure is worth GBP 10,000 to the commissioner and each further one GBP 50 less; the provider's unit cost is GBP 4,000 or GBP 5,000 with equal probability. The virtual cost of the high-cost type is 5 + 1 x 1 = 6, so it produces 80 rather than its first-best 100, and the low-cost type's rent is 1 x 80 = 80 (GBP 80,000). The transfers are GBP 560,000 and GBP 400,000.

Expected result TRUE for every worked example. In the ENHANCED example a cell that caps savings before sharing returns 36,000,000, a cell with no limit returns 54,000,000 and the cell doubled or halved returns 96,000,000 or 24,000,000, each FALSE. Type test case
has absolute tolerance 0.5

has description in the module A cheaper option costs £9,000 and produces 4.0 QALYs, against current care at £12,000 and 4.2 QALYs. Incremental cost is minus £3,000 and incremental effect is minus 0.2 QALYs, so the ratio is £15,000. Because the incremental effect is negative, the ratio is the saving per QALY forgone.
